title: Two Pointers Check
description: Opposite-end movement and sorted pair sums.

questions.prompt: For sorted `[1, 2, 4, 7, 11]` and target `9`, after `1+11=12` you should:
questions.explanation: Sum too big → shrink the right end (`R--`) for a smaller partner.

questions.prompt: Opposite-end pair sum on a sorted array typically runs in:
questions.explanation: Each step moves one pointer; at most `n` steps → `O(n)`.

questions.prompt: Opposite-end pair tricks usually require the array to be:
questions.explanation: Ordering lets you discard one end safely when the sum is too big or too small.

questions.prompt: When `L >= R` and no pair matched, the correct conclusion is:

options.text: A pair exists but was skipped
No two distinct indices sum to the target
You must start over with nested loops

questions.explanation: Pointers crossing means every useful opposite-end combination was considered.
